channel.title: Israel National News Flashes
channel.description: Latest news flashes from Israel National News

item.title: Nepal flood disaster: 590 foreign nationals still missing
item.description:
Nepal's Foreign Ministry has updated the number of foreign nationals still missing following the floods which struck the country, saying that 590 people remain unaccounted for.
The missing individuals are citizens of 39 different countries. So far, 323 foreign nationals have been rescued.

item.description: Inspectors uncover 100 bottles hidden inside drinks at Kerem Shalom; truck seized and Israeli company’s Gaza aid permit suspended.

item.description: Police open kidnapping investigation after Petah Tikva boy vanishes; Jerusalem suspect found is arrested and jailed.

item.description: Rabbi Ovadia Yosef’s daughters, Rivka Chikotai and Adina Bar-Shalom, sharply criticize Shas, accusing the party and Aryeh Deri of abandoning their father’s legacy.

item.description: Court awards NIS 180,000 to three Jews attacked by an Arab mob near the Lions’ Gate during Operation Guardian of the Walls.

item.title: Corruption raid: Council head arrested in massive police operation
item.description: Seven arrested and six detained as police probe bribery, rigged tenders and alleged fictitious employees used to siphon public funds.

item.title: Canadian sites display 'Lake America' despite Google’s US-only change
item.description: Several Canadian websites mistakenly display “Lake America" after Google renames Lake Ontario in the US in accordance with Trump executive order.

item.title: IRGC: We shot down US MQ-9 drone over Strait of Hormuz
item.description:
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) claimed it shot down a US MQ-9 Reaper drone over the Strait of Hormuz.
The claim has not yet been confirmed by the United States.

item.title: Likud primary fraud claims | After recount, Gamliel drops to 35th place
item.description: Two weeks after the Likud primary and amid fraud allegations, the party releases final results, placing Eti Atiya 25th and Gila Gamliel 35th.

item.title: Retired cops urge Mamdani to skip 9/11 memorial
item.description: Retired Port Authority officers urge NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani to skip the 25th anniversary 9/11 ceremony, warning his presence could cause pain.

item.title: Khamenei calls US and Israel 'sworn enemies' of Muslim unity
item.description: Iranian Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei calls the US and Israel “sworn enemies" of Muslim unity and urges greater solidarity across the Muslim world.

item.title: Netanyahu backs Smotrich plan: We will bring the farm revolution to the Negev and Galilee
item.description: The Prime Minister says he would promote the establishment of agricultural farms, stressing the national importance of strengthening Jewish presence in the Negev and Galilee.

item.title: Trump: If I weren’t President, there would probably be no Middle East
item.description: Speaking on Fox News, President Donald Trump says Iran cannot have a nuclear weapon, touting the US blockade and military campaign while warning of catastrophic regional consequences.

item.title: Secret defense deal | Confidential agreement between Finland and Israel revealed
item.description: A confidential memorandum of understanding between the two countries outlines closer defense coordination through 2034, including research, development and military procurement.

item.title: Bessent: Trump administration preparing new bank sanctions over Iran
item.description: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent says the Trump administration plans new bank sanctions as Washington intensifies efforts to isolate Iran economically.

item.title: Jordanian military: We intercepted eight missiles that entered our airspace
item.description:
The Jordanian military announced that it had intercepted eight missiles that entered the country's airspace.
The statement came after Iran claimed responsibility for an attack on two US military bases in Jordan.

item.title: Britain's Chief Rabbi warns sanctions over E1 could harm British Jews
item.description: Rabbi Sir Ephraim Mirvis warns planned UK sanctions over Israeli construction in E1 could harm British Jews, trade ties and prospects for Middle East peace.

item.description: Amcha Yisrael chairman Ofer Winter responds to the Prime Minister’s claim that his party poses a “danger" to the right: “We are part of the right-wing camp, but we work for no one."

item.title: Man seriously injured in violent incident in Tel Aviv
item.description:
A man in his 50s was seriously injured in a violent incident in Tel Aviv.
Magen David Adom (MDA) medics treated him at the scene before evacuating him to Ichilov Hospital in the city.
